candidate_relations.scope_detail: Biochemical/clinical thyroid hormone excess without etiology

candidate_relations.reason: This describes a possible psychiatric consequence of the thyroid disorder rather than Graves disease itself.
Mood disturbance may describe part of the presentation but is not the etiologic thyroid diagnosis.
A manic episode may account for the behavioral presentation but is a manifestation of the underlying Graves-related thyrotoxicosis.
Anxiety is present but does not identify the benchmark thyroid disease.
A TSH-secreting pituitary tumor would generally produce inappropriately normal or elevated TSH, conflicting with the markedly suppressed TSH and Graves benchmark.
Hyperthyroidism is established but is less specific than Graves disease.
Thyroid storm asserts a severe acute crisis not supported by the afebrile, subacute presentation without major systemic decompensation.
Psychotic symptoms can accompany thyrotoxicosis, but psychotic disorder is not the underlying Graves diagnosis; delusions were also not held with psychotic intensity.
This is a possible neuropsychiatric manifestation rather than Graves disease itself.
Pheochromocytoma does not explain the documented severe primary thyrotoxicosis and goitre and is distinct from Graves disease.
The manic presentation may be secondary to thyrotoxicosis but does not specify the underlying Graves disease.
Thyroiditis is a different etiology from Graves disease and is less consistent with the smooth non-tender goitre and prolonged severe thyrotoxicosis.
Thyrotoxic crisis asserts an acute decompensated state unsupported by the afebrile, months-long course without organ failure.
Graves' disease is a harmless wording variant of the benchmark Graves disease.
Mania describes the prominent behavioral manifestation but not the underlying Graves disease.
Bipolar disorder is distinct from Graves disease and the record instead documents marked thyrotoxicosis temporally associated with the manic symptoms.
Schizophrenia is a separate diagnosis and is not supported by the subacute thyrotoxic presentation or the absence of sustained psychotic-intensity delusions.
Thyroid disease includes Graves disease but omits the required specific etiology and hyperthyroid subtype.
